To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
occupation and harassment in the workplace are important factors associated alcohol use and misuse.

occupation and workplace harassment are associated with alcohol use, but the role of occupation is modestly moderated and mediated/suppressed by family situation, social support, and other personal characteristics.

occupation and work organization factors are important factors associated to alcohol use and that the effects of occupation and work environment on alcohol use and misuse are mediated by family situation, social support network, and personal characteristics.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the social determinants of health, and it shows how social determinants are associated with alcohol use, misuse and related health outcomes.
the specific contribution of the work environment to alcohol use and abuse, and not with the contribution of alcohol abuse to work environment.
the social determinants of alcohol use and misuse and the role of the workplace in this process.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the workplace is a significant factor associated with alcohol use, but its impact is modest compared to other factors, and it is moderated by other factors.

the workplace is a social environment in which alcohol consumption is a common and acceptable practice, and where alcohol consumption is a coping mechanism used to deal with the stress associated with the constraints of the job and the workplace.
alcohol use and misuse is the product of agent personality, structures (work and non-work) of daily life, macro social structures, and workplace harassment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the workplace is not the only source of stress, but it is a significant source of stress.
the workplace is a context in which the use of alcohol is influenced by the interaction of individual and contextual factors.
the workplace is an important context, but not a determinant of alcohol use and misuse.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the workplace should be considered in the prevention of alcohol use and misuse.
the social action model of health is an appropriate framework for studying alcohol use and misuse.
the workplace can be a source of both stress and resources.
